description: List the Granola folders this API key can see, one page at a time, as the options a person picks from. Each option's id is the folder id granola-list_notes-1 takes as folder_id, and that filter already includes the folder's child folders. Pass the returned next_cursor back as `cursor` to read the next page; a null next_cursor means the last page. This is the browse node behind the granola sync picker, so its output is the scope-option shape.

parent_id.description: Ignored. This node lists every folder in one flat page; see quirks.

query.description: Ignored. GET /v1/folders takes no text filter.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

limit.description: Folders per page, 1 to 30. Granola defaults to 10.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as cursor to read the next page. Null on the last page.

response_schema.description: GET /v1/folders. Lenient on purpose. Granola's OpenAPI document marks id, object, name and parent_folder_id all required, but a node that dies on a vendor's new null returns nothing at all.

quirks: No code: the whole call is a declarative http mapping. The provider's own cursor and page size are its query parameters, so the runtime's paginate record expresses them, and the mapping renames `cursor` to `next_cursor` on the way out.

Flat, not a tree, even though a folder carries parent_folder_id. One page holds every folder a key can see whatever its depth, and granola-list_notes-1 already includes a folder's child folders when it filters on folder_id, so picking a parent picks what is under it. A nested picker would be a v2 that pages per parent.
GET /v1/folders takes no text filter, so `query` is accepted and ignored. Granola pages at 30 folders, so the picker filters what it has fetched.
The whole list is what the key can see: a personal key reaches private folders shared with the person, a workspace key reaches the spaces granted API access. See app.json auth.key_permissions.
